new_results.statement: Every cap-one probability density is an L1 limit of finite convex mixtures of indicators of bounded finite unions of intervals of measure one; therefore bounded product kernels have the same supremum on arbitrary cap-one product laws and on such product indicators, without an attained optimizer or bounded fragment count.

For a rank-two physical two-hub cross bank B with arbitrary diagonal leaf twists and max leverage h<1, ||p_Q||inf <=4/((2-q)sqrt(q)) det(BB^T)^(-1/4) for max(1,2h)<=q<2; optimized constant is 4 for h<=1/2 and 2/((1-h)sqrt(2h)) for h>1/2.
For D=det(BB^T), Delta_jk=det(b_j,b_k), leverage ell_j satisfies sum_{k!=j}Delta_jk^2=ell_j D and residual pair volume=(1-ell_j)D.

A high slab-ratio witness retaining substantial diagonal two-hub Gram determinant must have max leverage tending to one, with >half of all squared 2x2 cross volume on one physical leaf star and non-star volume <=2 D^(3/4)/R.
For three mutually uncoupled physical leaves, ||p_Q||inf <=3*2^(1/6)(|det(b1,b2)| ||b3||)^(-1/3), with arbitrary diagonal leaf curvature and outside terms.
At slab ratio R, every transverse nonedge pair above threshold delta>3*2^(1/6)/R dominates all other delta-active leaves in the nonzero leaf-curvature graph.
